cim: The women redefining AI across the Asia-Pacific
cim_eredeti: The women redefining AI across the Asia-Pacific
szoveg_eredeti:
Female leaders at Finoverse, HashKey and Lirvana Labs are ensuring women don’t just adapt to artificial intelligence, but actively design the rules and tools behind it

Asia-Pacific is embracing artificial intelligence more actively than the rest of the world. A 2025 Boston Consulting Group survey found 70 per cent of frontline workers in the region use AI regularly compared to 51 per cent globally, while 60 per cent felt optimistic about its potential against 52 per cent worldwide.

Enthusiasm does not mean equal opportunity, however. Singapore-based gender advocacy group Nineby9 warns that women face a double disadvantage as AI reshapes work: they are concentrated in clerical, administrative and business-support roles exposed to automation, plus they remain under-represented in the jobs AI is enhancing or creating anew. The challenge, then, is to help women adapt to AI while expanding their influence over the technologies and rules shaping the future economy.

Christie Pang, co-founder of education technology company Lirvana Labs, believes training young women is a crucial first step. She wants female graduates and entry-level workers to have access to AI skills so they can compete for emerging opportunities and generate long-term value.

Her emphasis on human capability also shapes product development at Lirvana. Educators help design Yeti Confetti, the company’s AI-powered platform, rather than being expected to adapt to a finished product. “Giving someone a sharp scalpel does not make them a heart surgeon,” she says. “Training matters.”

Anna Liu worked as a lawyer at Skadden and Tencent before becoming CEO of HashKey RWA, a virtual asset trading platform. For her, technical expertise is not the only route towards influence. She calls her traditional legal training “the single most useful tool” she has brought to her role. Her advice to women entering emerging-technology fields is to combine depth with breadth: “What matters is how deeply you understand your field and how broadly you can see.”
